Proofpoint vs Mimecast vs Microsoft Defender for Office 365

The Definitive Email Security Showdown 2026

20 min read Hands-on Tested (Mimecast, Microsoft) Gartner Leader Analysis January 2026
Harish G
Security Researcher | Hands-on with Mimecast & Microsoft Defender
    <div class="content">
        <img src="/images/comparisons/email-security-comparison.png"
            alt="Proofpoint vs Mimecast vs Microsoft Defender Email Security Comparison" class="featured-image" loading="lazy">

        <!-- METHODOLOGY -->
        <div class="methodology-box">
            <h3 style="margin-top: 0; color: var(--accent-cyan);"><i class="fas fa-microscope"></i> Hybrid
                Methodology: Personal Experience + Industry Research</h3>
            <p style="margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">
                This comparison combines <strong>hands-on operational experience</strong> with Mimecast and
                Microsoft Defender for Office 365, plus comprehensive research on Proofpoint. Unlike pure research
                articles, I've personally managed email security operations using two of these three platforms.
            </p>
            <p style="margin-bottom: 0;">My analysis is backed by:</p>
            <ul style="margin-bottom: 0;">
                <li><strong>Personal Experience:</strong> Daily operations with Mimecast and Microsoft Defender for
                    O365</li>
                <li><strong>2025 Gartner Magic Quadrant</strong> for Email Security Platforms</li>
                <li><strong>G2 Reviews:</strong> 1,500+ verified user reviews across all three platforms</li>
                <li><strong>Reddit & Community Feedback:</strong> r/sysadmin, r/cybersecurity discussions</li>
                <li><strong>Official Documentation:</strong> Vendor feature specifications and release notes</li>
            </ul>
        </div>

        <!-- EXECUTIVE SUMMARY -->
        <h2>Executive Summary</h2>
        <p>
            After extensive hands-on experience with Mimecast and Microsoft Defender for Office 365, combined with
            thorough research on Proofpoint, I can share real-world insights that go beyond marketing materials.
            Each platform has distinct strengths and weaknesses that matter in day-to-day security operations.
        </p>

        <div class="warning-box">
            <p style="margin: 0;"><strong><i class="fas fa-lightbulb"></i> The Real Question:</strong>
                Most "comparisons" online treat these as equivalent solutions. They're not. <strong>Proofpoint and
                    Mimecast are Secure Email Gateways (SEGs)</strong> that sit in front of your mail flow, while
                <strong>Microsoft Defender is an API-integrated solution</strong> that works alongside Exchange
                Online Protection (EOP). This architectural difference fundamentally changes how you deploy, manage,
                and troubleshoot each solution.
            </p>
        </div>

        <table>
            <thead>
                <tr>
                    <th>Platform</th>
                    <th>Architecture</th>
                    <th>Gartner 2025</th>
                    <th>Best For</th>
                    <th>My Verdict</th>
                </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
                <tr>
                    <td><strong style="color: var(--proofpoint-red);">Proofpoint</strong></td>
                    <td>SEG (MX record change)</td>
                    <td>Leader (#1 in Ability to Execute)</td>
                    <td>Enterprise compliance & threat intel</td>
                    <td class="runner-up">Best Threat Intel</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td><strong style="color: var(--mimecast-green);">Mimecast</strong></td>
                    <td>SEG (MX record change)</td>
                    <td>Leader (Strong all-rounder)</td>
                    <td>Reporting, message tracing, archiving</td>
                    <td class="winner"><i class="fas fa-trophy"></i> Best UX & Operations</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td><strong style="color: var(--microsoft-blue);">Microsoft Defender</strong></td>
                    <td>API + EOP integration</td>
                    <td>Leader (Deep M365 integration)</td>
                    <td>Microsoft-heavy environments</td>
                    <td class="third">Best Value (with E5)</td>
                </tr>
            </tbody>
        </table>

        <!-- ARCHITECTURE DEEP DIVE -->
        <h2><i class="fas fa-network-wired"></i> Architecture Deep Dive: Why It Matters</h2>

        <p>Before comparing features, you need to understand <em>how</em> these solutions process email. This
            determines everything from deployment complexity to troubleshooting workflows.</p>

        <h3>Secure Email Gateway (SEG) Architecture: Proofpoint & Mimecast</h3>

        <div class="info-box">
            <p style="margin: 0;"><strong><i class="fas fa-route"></i> Mail Flow:</strong>
                Internet → <strong>SEG (Proofpoint/Mimecast)</strong> → Microsoft 365 → User Inbox</p>
            <p style="margin: 0.5rem 0 0 0; font-size: 0.9rem; color: var(--text-muted);">
                Your MX records point to the SEG. All inbound email is inspected <em>before</em> reaching Microsoft
                365. Outbound mail is also routed through the SEG for DLP and encryption.
            </p>
        </div>

        <p><strong>Operational Implications:</strong></p>
        <ul>
            <li><strong>Full visibility:</strong> Every email passes through your security layer first. You see
                everything, even messages blocked before they reach M365.</li>
            <li><strong>Redundancy:</strong> SEGs typically maintain queues if M365 is down. Mimecast's continuity
                feature lets users send/receive email even during Exchange outages.</li>
            <li><strong>Complexity:</strong> You're managing two mail flows. SPF/DKIM/DMARC configurations require
                careful alignment between SEG and M365.</li>
            <li><strong>Latency:</strong> Additional hop adds ~100-500ms to email delivery (usually imperceptible,
                but can affect real-time workflows).</li>
        </ul>

        <h3>API-Integrated Architecture: Microsoft Defender for Office 365</h3>

        <div class="industry-box">
            <div class="label"><i class="fas fa-route"></i> Mail Flow</div>
            <p style="margin: 0;">Internet → Microsoft 365 (EOP + MDO) → User Inbox</p>
            <p style="margin: 0.5rem 0 0 0; font-size: 0.9rem;">
                Exchange Online Protection (EOP) handles basic filtering. Defender for Office 365 adds advanced
                threat protection via API integration. No MX record change required.
            </p>
        </div>

        <p><strong>Operational Implications:</strong></p>
        <ul>
            <li><strong>Seamless integration:</strong> No separate vendor to manage. Everything in the Microsoft 365
                admin ecosystem.</li>
            <li><strong>Single point of failure:</strong> If M365 has issues, you have no email continuity (unless
                you add a third-party solution).</li>
            <li><strong>Simpler deployment:</strong> Flip a license switch. No DNS changes, no connector
                configuration.</li>
            <li><strong>Less visibility:</strong> You only see what Microsoft shows you. Third-party threats blocked
                by EOP may not appear in your Defender reports.</li>
        </ul>

        <div class="success-box">
            <p style="margin: 0;"><strong><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> My Take:</strong>
                For organizations with <strong>dedicated security teams</strong> who want maximum control and
                visibility, SEG architecture (Proofpoint/Mimecast) is superior. For <strong>lean IT teams</strong>
                who prioritize simplicity and are already deep in the Microsoft ecosystem, Defender's native
                integration is compelling.</p>
        </div>

        <!-- DETAILED COMPARISON -->
        <h2><i class="fas fa-envelope-open-text"></i> Feature-by-Feature Comparison</h2>

        <h3>1. Message Tracing & Visibility</h3>

        <p>Message tracing is where you'll spend significant time during incident response and user support. The
            quality of this feature directly impacts your operational efficiency.</p>

        <div class="personal-box">
            <div class="label"><i class="fas fa-user-check"></i> Personal Experience - Mimecast</div>
            <p>Mimecast's message tracing is <strong>exceptional</strong>. The Tracking feature in the
                Administration Console provides:</p>
            <ul style="margin-bottom: 0;">
                <li><strong>Sub-second search:</strong> Query millions of messages instantly with filters for
                    sender, recipient, subject, date range, and delivery status</li>
                <li><strong>Complete journey visibility:</strong> See every processing step—receipt, scanning,
                    policy evaluation, delivery attempt, bounce handling</li>
                <li><strong>Header inspection:</strong> Full email headers available without PowerShell or export
                </li>
                <li><strong>Release with one click:</strong> If a message is quarantined, release it directly from
                    the trace results</li>
            </ul>
            <p style="margin-top: 0.5rem; margin-bottom: 0;"><em>Real scenario:</em> User reports "I didn't receive
                an email from client X." In Mimecast, I search by sender, see it was quarantined due to a failed SPF
                check, verify it's legitimate, release it, and whitelist the sender domain—all in under 60 seconds.
            </p>
        </div>

        <div class="industry-box">
            <div class="label"><i class="fas fa-user-check"></i> Personal Experience - Microsoft Defender</div>
            <p>Microsoft's message trace in the Exchange Admin Center is functional but <strong>significantly more
                    limited</strong>:</p>
            <ul style="margin-bottom: 0;">
                <li><strong>10-day limit:</strong> Detailed message trace only works for the last 10 days. Beyond
                    that, you must use <code>Start-HistoricalSearch</code> cmdlet which takes hours to complete.
                </li>
                <li><strong>1000 message cap:</strong> Results are limited to 1000 messages per query</li>
                <li><strong>Slow interface:</strong> Complex queries can take 30+ seconds to return</li>
                <li><strong>Split portals:</strong> You may need to check EAC for trace, Security portal for threat
                    details, and Compliance portal for retention</li>
            </ul>
            <div class="source-citation">
                <strong>PowerShell workaround:</strong>
                <code>Get-MessageTrace -SenderAddress user@domain.com -StartDate (Get-Date).AddDays(-10)</code><br>
                For historical:
                <code>Start-HistoricalSearch -ReportTitle "Investigation" -StartDate "01/01/2026" -EndDate "01/15/2026" -ReportType MessageTrace</code>
            </div>
        </div>

        <div class="info-box">
            <p style="margin: 0;"><strong><i class="fas fa-search"></i> Proofpoint Smart Search:</strong>
                Proofpoint's Smart Search provides 90+ days of searchable message logs with advanced filtering. The
                interface is clean but more complex than Mimecast. Key advantage: Deep integration with Proofpoint
                TAP (Targeted Attack Protection) means you can pivot from a suspicious message to full threat
                analysis in one click.</p>
        </div>

        <table>
            <thead>
                <tr>
                    <th>Message Tracing Feature</th>
                    <th>Proofpoint</th>
                    <th>Mimecast</th>
                    <th>Microsoft</th>
                </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
                <tr>
                    <td>Real-time tracking</td>
                    <td><i class="fas fa-check check-icon"></i> Yes</td>
                    <td><i class="fas fa-check check-icon"></i> Excellent</td>
                    <td><i class="fas fa-check check-icon"></i> Basic</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>Search speed</td>
                    <td>Fast</td>
                    <td class="winner">Fastest</td>
                    <td>Slow</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>Historical retention (portal)</td>
                    <td>90+ days</td>
                    <td class="winner">Configurable (years)</td>
                    <td>10 days detailed</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>Results limit per query</td>
                    <td>10,000+</td>
                    <td class="winner">Unlimited</td>
                    <td>1,000</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>PowerShell required for advanced</td>
                    <td>No</td>
                    <td>No</td>
                    <td><i class="fas fa-times x-icon"></i> Yes</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>Header inspection in UI</td>
                    <td><i class="fas fa-check check-icon"></i></td>
                    <td><i class="fas fa-check check-icon"></i></td>
                    <td><i class="fas fa-minus partial-icon"></i> Limited</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>One-click release from quarantine</td>
                    <td><i class="fas fa-check check-icon"></i></td>
                    <td><i class="fas fa-check check-icon"></i></td>
                    <td><i class="fas fa-check check-icon"></i></td>
                </tr>
            </tbody>
        </table>

        <h3>2. Reporting & Analytics</h3>

        <div class="personal-box">
            <div class="label"><i class="fas fa-chart-bar"></i> Personal Experience - Mimecast</div>
            <p style="margin-bottom: 0;">
                Mimecast's reporting is where it truly shines. The dashboards are <strong>intuitive, visually
                    appealing, and actionable</strong>. I can quickly generate executive-ready reports on threat
                trends, user behavior, and policy effectiveness. The reports are easy to schedule, export, and share
                with stakeholders. This is one of the biggest advantages I've experienced versus Microsoft.
            </p>
        </div>

        <div class="industry-box">
            <div class="label"><i class="fas fa-chart-bar"></i> Personal Experience - Microsoft Defender</div>
            <p style="margin-bottom: 0;">
                Microsoft's reporting is <strong>scattered and less intuitive</strong>. Reports are spread across
                the Security portal, Compliance portal, and Exchange admin center. The Threat Protection Status
                report is useful but limited to 90 days for charts and 30 days for detail tables. Creating
                executive-ready reports requires manual effort or third-party tools.
            </p>
            <div class="source-citation">
                <strong>Source:</strong> <a
                    href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/reports-email-security"
                    target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Microsoft Docs</a> confirms report date range limitations and the
                fragmented portal experience.
            </div>
        </div>

        <div class="warning-box">
            <p style="margin: 0;"><strong><i class="fas fa-exclamation-triangle"></i> Industry Feedback on Microsoft
                    Reporting:</strong> Multiple sources note that Microsoft Defender can flood administrators with
                Threat Analytics alerts, and the "Action recommended" notifications often don't specify what action
                is needed, creating confusion.</p>
            <div class="source-citation">

        <h3>3. Email Archiving & Data Retention</h3>

        <div class="personal-box">
            <div class="label"><i class="fas fa-archive"></i> Personal Experience - Mimecast</div>
            <p style="margin-bottom: 0;">
                Mimecast Cloud Archive is <strong>purpose-built for compliance and eDiscovery</strong>. You get
                unlimited retention periods, tamper-proof storage, and fast search across years of archived emails.
                For organizations with regulatory requirements (HIPAA, GDPR, financial compliance), this is a major
                differentiator.
            </p>
        </div>

        <div class="industry-box">
            <div class="label"><i class="fas fa-archive"></i> Personal Experience - Microsoft</div>
            <p style="margin-bottom: 0;">
                Microsoft 365 has archiving via the Compliance Center, but it's <strong>not at the same
                    level</strong> as dedicated solutions like Mimecast. You get archive mailboxes and retention
                policies, but search performance degrades with large datasets, and the eDiscovery experience is
                clunkier. Organizations with serious compliance needs often supplement with third-party archiving.
            </p>
        </div>

        <h3>4. Threat Detection & Prevention</h3>

        <p>This is where the technical differences become critical. All three are Gartner Leaders, but their
            detection architectures and capabilities differ significantly.</p>

        <h4><i class="fas fa-shield-alt" style="color: var(--proofpoint-red);"></i> Proofpoint: The Threat
            Intelligence Powerhouse</h4>

        <div class="success-box">
            <p><strong>Proofpoint's Detection Stack:</strong></p>
            <ul style="margin-bottom: 0;">
                <li><strong>Nexus AI:</strong> Large language models trained on billions of email samples detect
                    semantic patterns in BEC attacks that rule-based systems miss</li>
                <li><strong>Supplier Risk:</strong> Builds relationship graphs to detect when a "supplier" email
                    doesn't match historical communication patterns</li>
                <li><strong>TAP (Targeted Attack Protection):</strong> Multi-stage sandboxing with URL
                    rewriting—clicks are analyzed at time-of-click, not just time-of-delivery</li>
                <li><strong>Very Attacked People (VAP):</strong> Identifies your most-targeted users and applies
                    enhanced protection automatically</li>
                <li><strong>QR Code Analysis:</strong> Scans QR codes in attachments and images—a growing attack
                    vector that many solutions miss</li>
            </ul>
            <div class="source-citation">
                <strong>Detection Rate:</strong> Proofpoint claims 99.99% threat block rate. Independent testing by
                SE Labs (2024) rated Proofpoint AAA with 100% detection of email-borne threats.
            </div>
        </div>

        <h4><i class="fas fa-shield-alt" style="color: var(--mimecast-green);"></i> Mimecast: Balanced Protection
            with Operational Excellence</h4>

        <div class="personal-box">
            <div class="label"><i class="fas fa-user-check"></i> Personal Experience</div>
            <p><strong>Mimecast's Detection Stack:</strong></p>
            <ul style="margin-bottom: 0;">
                <li><strong>Cybergraph AI:</strong> Identity graph technology that maps organizational relationships
                    to detect impersonation</li>
                <li><strong>URL Protect:</strong> Real-time URL scanning with configurable click-time vs
                    delivery-time analysis</li>
                <li><strong>Attachment Protect:</strong> Static and dynamic analysis with configurable sandbox
                    timeout</li>
                <li><strong>Internal Email Protect:</strong> Scans internal-to-internal emails for compromised
                    account detection (unique differentiator)</li>
                <li><strong>Brand Exploit Protect:</strong> Monitors for domain spoofing and brand impersonation
                    across the web (add-on)</li>
            </ul>
            <p style="margin-top: 0.5rem; margin-bottom: 0;"><em>Real-world observation:</em> In my experience,
                Mimecast catches ~95% of phishing attempts on first pass. The remaining 5% typically get flagged
                within hours via retrospective URL scanning as threat intelligence updates.</p>
        </div>

        <h4><i class="fas fa-shield-alt" style="color: var(--microsoft-blue);"></i> Microsoft Defender for Office
            365: Native Integration with Limitations</h4>

        <div class="industry-box">
            <div class="label"><i class="fas fa-user-check"></i> Personal Experience</div>
            <p><strong>Defender's Detection Stack:</strong></p>
            <ul style="margin-bottom: 0;">
                <li><strong>Safe Links:</strong> URL rewriting and time-of-click protection. Works well but you
                    can't customize the detonation timeout.</li>
                <li><strong>Safe Attachments:</strong> Sandboxing with 3 modes—Dynamic Delivery (preview body, delay
                    attachment), Block, Monitor</li>
                <li><strong>Anti-phishing policies:</strong> Impersonation protection for users and domains.
                    Requires manual configuration for each protected identity.</li>
                <li><strong>ZAP (Zero-hour Auto Purge):</strong> Retroactively removes malicious emails from inboxes
                    after delivery—this is genuinely excellent and often underappreciated</li>
            </ul>
            <p style="margin-top: 0.5rem; margin-bottom: 0;"><em>Honest assessment:</em> Defender is "good enough"
                for most organizations. But "good enough" isn't the same as "best." I've seen Defender miss
                sophisticated BEC attacks that Proofpoint or Mimecast would catch. The gap is narrowing, but it
                exists.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="warning-box">
            <p style="margin: 0;"><strong><i class="fas fa-exclamation-triangle"></i> The Hidden Danger of
                    Defender:</strong>
                Because Defender is native to M365, many organizations assume they're protected by default. They're
                not. <strong>EOP (Exchange Online Protection)</strong> is the default—it provides basic spam/malware
                filtering. <strong>Defender for Office 365</strong> (Plan 1 or Plan 2) requires additional licensing
                and configuration. I've audited organizations who thought they had "Microsoft security" only to
                discover they were running on EOP alone.</p>
        </div>

        <h3>5. Pricing & Total Cost of Ownership</h3>

        <p>Email security pricing is notoriously opaque. All three vendors provide quote-based pricing for
            enterprises, making direct comparisons challenging. Here's a breakdown based on publicly available data,
            user reports, and industry experience:</p>

        <h4><i class="fas fa-money-bill-wave" style="color: var(--proofpoint-red);"></i> Proofpoint Pricing</h4>

        <div class="success-box">
            <p><strong>Proofpoint Licensing Tiers:</strong></p>
            <ul style="margin-bottom: 0;">
                <li><strong>Proofpoint Essentials:</strong> ~$2.50-5/user/month. SMB-focused, basic email security,
                    no TAP</li>
                <li><strong>Proofpoint Advanced:</strong> ~$4-8/user/month. Adds TAP sandboxing, URL defense</li>
                <li><strong>Proofpoint Complete:</strong> ~$8-15/user/month. Full suite: archiving, continuity,
                    security awareness</li>
                <li><strong>Enterprise Bundles:</strong> Custom pricing, typically $25-70/user/year for large
                    organizations</li>
            </ul>
            <p style="margin-top: 0.5rem; margin-bottom: 0;"><strong>Hidden costs:</strong> Proofpoint add-ons (DLP,
                TRAP, CASB) are separately licensed. Budget 20-40% more than base quotes for full functionality.</p>
        </div>

        <h4><i class="fas fa-money-bill-wave" style="color: var(--mimecast-green);"></i> Mimecast Pricing</h4>

        <div class="personal-box">
            <div class="label"><i class="fas fa-dollar-sign"></i> Personal Experience</div>
            <p><strong>Mimecast Licensing Approach:</strong></p>
            <ul style="margin-bottom: 0;">
                <li><strong>Email Security - Cloud Gateway:</strong> ~$3-5/user/month. Core email filtering and
                    protection</li>
                <li><strong>Targeted Threat Protection (TTP):</strong> ~$2-4/user/month add-on. URL Protect,
                    Attachment Protect, Impersonation Protect</li>
                <li><strong>Cloud Archive:</strong> ~$3-6/user/month add-on. Depends on retention period</li>
                <li><strong>Full Suite:</strong> ~$8-12/user/month when bundled</li>
            </ul>
            <p style="margin-top: 0.5rem; margin-bottom: 0;"><em>Budget reality:</em> In my experience, a
                fully-featured Mimecast deployment costs $6-10/user/month for mid-size organizations. Negotiation
                matters—multi-year contracts can reduce this by 15-25%.</p>
        </div>

        <h4><i class="fas fa-money-bill-wave" style="color: var(--microsoft-blue);"></i> Microsoft Defender Pricing
        </h4>

        <div class="industry-box">
            <div class="label"><i class="fas fa-user-check"></i> Personal Experience</div>
            <p><strong>Microsoft Licensing Complexity:</strong></p>
            <ul style="margin-bottom: 0;">
                <li><strong>Exchange Online Protection (EOP):</strong> Included with all Microsoft 365 plans. Basic
                    protection only.</li>
                <li><strong>Defender for Office 365 Plan 1:</strong> $2/user/month standalone. Safe Links, Safe
                    Attachments, anti-phishing</li>
                <li><strong>Defender for Office 365 Plan 2:</strong> $5/user/month standalone. Adds threat
                    investigation, AIR, attack simulation</li>
                <li><strong>Microsoft 365 E5:</strong> ~$57/user/month includes full Defender suite + Sentinel,
                    Entra ID P2, etc.</li>
            </ul>
            <p style="margin-top: 0.5rem; margin-bottom: 0;"><em>The E5 calculation:</em> If you're already on E5,
                Defender is "free." But that's only true if you'd pay for E5 anyway. Upgrading from E3 ($36/user) to
                E5 ($57/user) just for email security is expensive—$21/user/month more. Compare that to adding
                Mimecast at $8/user/month to your E3 license.</p>
        </div>

        <!-- VERDICT -->
        <h2><i class="fas fa-gavel"></i> The Verdict</h2>

        <p>After thousands of hours managing email security across different platforms, here's my honest assessment.
            The "best" solution depends entirely on your organization's specific context.</p>

        <div class="verdict-grid">
            <div class="verdict-card proofpoint">
                <h4><i class="fas fa-trophy"></i> Choose Proofpoint If...</h4>
                <ul>
                    <li>You're a <strong>Fortune 500 or highly-regulated enterprise</strong> (financial services,
                        healthcare, legal)</li>
                    <li><strong>BEC protection is mission-critical</strong>—you handle wire transfers, M&A, or
                        executive communications that attackers target</li>
                    <li>You need <strong>best-in-class threat intelligence</strong> with Nexus AI and Very Attacked
                        People (VAP) analysis</li>
                    <li>You have <strong>budget for premium security</strong> and dedicated security staff to
                        maximize the platform</li>
                    <li>Compliance requirements demand <strong>extensive audit trails and forensic
                            capabilities</strong></li>
                </ul>
                <div class="verdict-badge">Best for: Large enterprises, regulated industries, threat intelligence
                    depth</div>
            </div>

            <div class="verdict-card mimecast">
                <h4><span class="crown"><i class="fas fa-crown"></i></span> Choose Mimecast If...</h4>
                <ul>
                    <li>You're a <strong>mid-market organization (500-10,000 employees)</strong> that needs
                        enterprise features without enterprise complexity</li>
                    <li><strong>Operational efficiency matters</strong>—you want IT admins to spend less time
                        troubleshooting email issues</li>
                    <li>You value <strong>exceptional message tracing and reporting</strong> for daily security
                        operations</li>
                    <li><strong>Email archiving and compliance</strong> are requirements (Cloud Archive is genuinely
                        excellent)</li>
                    <li>You want a <strong>SEG architecture</strong> for defense-in-depth but don't have Proofpoint
                        budget</li>
                </ul>
                <div class="verdict-badge">Best for: Mid-market, operations-focused teams, compliance-driven
                    organizations</div>
            </div>

            <div class="verdict-card microsoft">
                <h4><i class="fas fa-money-bill-wave"></i> Choose Microsoft Defender If...</h4>
                <ul>
                    <li>You're <strong>already on Microsoft 365 E5</strong> and don't want to pay for duplicate
                        functionality</li>
                    <li><strong>Unified Microsoft security stack</strong> is your strategy (Defender XDR, Sentinel,
                        Entra ID)</li>
                    <li>Your security team is <strong>comfortable with Microsoft portals</strong> and PowerShell for
                        advanced operations</li>
                    <li>Budget is constrained and <strong>"good enough" protection satisfies your risk
                            tolerance</strong></li>
                    <li>You're a <strong>smaller organization (under 500 users)</strong> where dedicated SEG
                        overhead isn't justified</li>
                </ul>
                <div class="verdict-badge">Best for: E5 customers, Microsoft-centric shops, budget-conscious
                    organizations</div>
            </div>
        </div>

                or Proofpoint as a SEG <em>in front of</em> Microsoft 365, while also licensing Defender for Office

                The SEG catches threats at the gateway, while Defender provides an additional layer with ZAP for
